sections.html:
Bills are mailed and collected by the Tax Commissioner in Moultrie. Value comes from the Tax Assessor's Office, and the commissioner controls neither value nor millage.

Visit 101 East Central Ave., Moultrie, GA 31768, or write to postal box 99. The office is staffed weekdays 8:00am to 4:30pm, and the property tax line is (229) 616-7410. The same office runs motor vehicle registration. Solid waste has its own desk at 101 East Central Avenue, Office 168, (229) 616-7405, and the landfill opens Saturdays from 8:00am to noon, handy when you are cleaning out a house before listing.

  • Tax Assessor's Office: appraisal, assessment notices and exemption approvals.
  • Board of Equalization: administrative appeals, with members named by the grand jury.
  • County commission and school board: each levies its own mill rate.
  • Tax Commissioner: bills, payments, liens and levies.

This is Southwest Georgia farm country, about 557 square miles, with the courthouse and the largest city in Moultrie. US 319 connects Moultrie to Interstate 75 roughly 24 miles east.

The 2025 population estimate is 47,438, and there are 19,775 housing units. Owner-occupants live in 63.7% of homes. A typical owned home is worth $121,400 and gross rent is $818. Those numbers help you judge where to price a listing.

December 10 is the normal deadline for real estate and business personal property, with bills mailed at least 60 days earlier. Go by the date your own bill prints, because it can shift.

The bill is addressed to the owner and not the lender. If your mortgage has no escrow, you must forward it yourself. The office cannot guarantee delivery, and interest, penalty and costs apply either way.

Mobile and manufactured homes run on their own deadline, so ask the Tax Commissioner what applies to yours. Moving one into or out of the county requires a relocation permit first, from the Compliance office in the Courthouse Annex, 229-616-7417.

Past the due date a bill picks up interest monthly and, later, a penalty. Rather than calculating it yourself, request a written payoff. Homesteaded property with a bill under $500 is spared the penalty.

If the tax stays unpaid, a tax lien called a FiFa goes on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court. It stays on a credit record for at least seven years, and the commissioner may levy and eventually sell the property. Levy is a last resort.

The office mails delinquent notices only at certain intervals, so the amount on the last notice you received may have grown by the time you pay or close.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax if the house sells?
sections.html:
Whoever owned the house on January 1 stays on the bill and any lien, even when the deed changes hands in June. A seller can shift that to the buyer by getting the closing statement to the commissioner within 90 days after the due date.

If your closing prorated the tax, carry the settlement statement to the office on East Central Avenue. The office can then record a lien against the new owner if the bill goes unpaid. Pass along to the buyer any bill that shows up for a house you have already sold.

Ask the title company how the county gets paid, then request a payoff from the commissioner dated near the closing. A recorded lien does not block a sale, because the payoff is settled at the closing table out of the sale funds. A cash buyer can close the same way and has no lender to satisfy first. For the closing, bring the deed, your latest bill and any lien paperwork.

Colquitt lists a standard exemption and several age, veteran and income-based ones, all subtracted from the assessed value, which Georgia fixes at 40% of fair market value. The first application goes to the Tax Assessor's Office, and first-time owners should bring a copy of the warranty deed. Georgia requires it to be received by April 1.

  • Standard homestead: $2,000 off assessed value, for county, school system and state levies.
  • Elderly school tax, age 62 or older: up to $10,000 off, with net income of $10,000 or less.
  • Elderly general, age 65 or older: up to $4,000 off, with a $10,000 income test that excludes Social Security and some retirement income.
  • Disabled veteran and qualifying surviving spouse: up to $63,780 off.
  • Floating exemption: age 62 or older with gross household income of $30,000 or less, covering state and county tax but not school tax.

Local exemptions override the state amounts when larger, so the assessors can tell you what applies today. Farmland has its own paths: assessment at 30% for bona fide agricultural use, and conservation use or timber programs that require a covenant of at least 10 years. Historic property and certain hazardous-site redevelopment parcels may also qualify. Owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less can defer tax until a sale or until the deferral and interest reach 85% of fair market value.

Write the appeal and file it within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. The choices are the equalization board or an arbitrator, and either result can go on to Superior Court.

Through April 1 each spring you may also file a return giving your own opinion of the property's January 1 value. Say nothing and you are treated as returning last year's value and exemptions. For a mobile home, the sequence is 45 days to appeal to the assessors, then 21 days from their notice to go to the equalization board.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Colquitt County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the Tax Commissioner's office, 101 East Central Ave., Moultrie, weekdays 8:00am to 4:30pm. Card payments carry a convenience fee from the card company.

faqs.q: What date is Colquitt County property tax normally due?
faqs.a: December 10 for real estate and business personal property. Trust the date printed on your bill, because it can change.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Colquitt County house with a recorded tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. The payoff is settled from the sale funds at closing, so request a current figure from the commissioner and hand it to the title company.

faqs.q: Which Colquitt County office takes homestead applications?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor's Office. Georgia requires the application to be received by April 1, and a later filing counts toward the next tax year.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window for a Colquitt County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the notice. You can ask for the equalization board or an arbitrator, and Superior Court is open afterward.
